Award.description: An award this event presents, with how many places.

note.description: Why the award skipped a higher-ranked eligible team; required when it did.

Ceremony.description: What the venue screen shows during the awards ceremony: only what has been revealed.

shown.description: How many slides have been revealed.

slides.description: The revealed slides, in ceremony order.

winners.description: Lowest place first, as they are read out.

place.description: "1st", "2nd"; empty for single-place awards and advancement.

Deliberation.description: Everything the judge advisor deliberates with, kept current on the `deliberation` topic.

advancement_slots.description: How many teams advance, from the event settings.

nominations.description: Candidates the judges selected on accepted rubrics.

EventSettings.description:
Per-event rules and timings. Stored as JSON on the event; missing fields take their defaults, so new
settings never break older events.

advancement_slots.description: How many teams advance to the next level of competition; 0 when none do.

gp_comment_required.description: A Gracious Professionalism score other than 3 needs a comment.

judging_match_gap_minutes.description: Minimum time between a team's judging session and any of its matches, used by schedule checks.

queue_call_minutes.description: How far ahead of a match a team should be queueing: its status becomes "Queue now".

queue_soon_minutes.description: How far ahead of a match a team is shown as "Soon", so queuers can find it before it is due.

rubric_review.description: Whether rubrics count straight away (a second one for a team waits) or wait for the judge advisor.

start_needs_ready.description: The match timer only starts once every team is ready, a no-show or scratched (the head referee can override).

team_agreement_required.description: The team confirms the scoresheet before it is submitted.

Feedback.description: The feedback page: "Great job" and "Think about" for each area.

GameTable.description: A competition table. Tables play in pairs by `sort_order`: positions 0 and 1 face each other, then 2 and 3.

Hundredths.description:
A score in hundredths of a point. Gracious Professionalism from four or five matches is scaled by 0.75 or
0.6, so Core Values can be fractional.

oneOf.description: A team is in two places at once.
A team's match is too close to its judging session.
A team has more or fewer ranking matches than the event has rounds.
Two matches use one table at the same time.
Two sessions use one pod at the same time.
A team's matches follow each other with little time between.
A team meets the same opponent in more than one ranking match.
A match or session is scheduled during a break, ceremony or meeting.
The schedule can't run as written.
It can run, but a team or volunteer will have a worse day.

JudgingSlot.description: One team in one pod in one judging session.

queue.description:
Where the team is: called, outside the room (`waiting`), in the room (`at_table`), in session
(`running`), done, or a no-show.

rubric.description: The team's rubric status: accepted if there is one, otherwise one waiting for review.

MatchSlot.description: One team at one table in one match.

queue.description: Where the team is on its way to this match.

queue_previous.description: The state before the last change, which undo returns to.

round.description: Which of the team's matches of this kind this is: 1 for its first ranking match, and so on.

sheet.description:
The slot's scoresheet: published if there is one, otherwise one waiting for review. Scores are not shown here,
because this topic is public.

oneOf.description: On deck: the next start of the match timer runs it.

MatchTimer.description:
The event's match timer. Live phases follow from `starts_at` and the clock, so every device computes the
same time remaining from one message.

match_ids.description: The matches this run is for.

starts_at.description: Match time zero, after any countdown.

Pod.description: A judging room or group of judges.

PodTimer.description: A pod's timer: which phase of which session it is in, and when that phase ends.

phase.description: Index into the session phases; `None` when the pod is idle.

phase_ms.description: The phase's length, including any minutes added.

Presence.description: A station device logged in with an access key and connected to the live feed right now.

connections.description: Open connections with this key (a reloaded tab can briefly have two).

waiting.description: Scoresheets and rubrics kept on the device that the server has not accepted yet, as the device reports.

oneOf.description: In the queue area beside the field, waiting to be sent to the table.
Not playing this match, by the head referee's decision.

RankingRow.description: One team's line on the scoreboard.

rank.description: Competition ranking: tied teams share a rank and the next rank is skipped (1, 1, 3).

scores.description: One entry per ranking round; `None` until the round has a published score.

Rubric.description: A stored rubric, as judges and the judge advisor see it.

duplicate.description: The team already has an accepted rubric.

ScheduleBlock.description: Something on the event timetable that is not a match or judging session: lunch, opening ceremony, briefings.

ScheduleIssue.description: One problem with the schedule. Its id follows from what it is about, so the same problem keeps its id.

team_id.description: The team this is about; `None` for event-wide issues such as a table used twice at once.

Scoresheet.description: A stored scoresheet, as head referees and referees see it.

issues.description: Warnings the season raised when the sheet arrived.

review_note.description: The head referee's note, shown to the referee when a sheet is rejected.

submitted_by.description: The login that sent it: `user:<name>` or `key:<label>`.

ScoresheetFlag.description: Why a sheet waits for the head referee even when the event publishes automatically.

oneOf.description: The team already has a published sheet for this round.
The season raised a warning, such as more seeds planted than released.
The device's total differed from the server's; the server's total was kept.
Valid sheets count straight away; the head referee sees flagged ones.
Every sheet waits for the head referee.
Waiting for the head referee.
Counts for ranking.
Replaced by a later sheet for the same round.

number.description: The team's FIRST number, as text ("1234").

TeamScores.description: One team's line of the spreadsheet's Results and Rankings page.

champions_score.description: Sum of the four ranks; lowest is best.

core_values.description: Core Values rows from both rubrics plus the Gracious Professionalism score.

oneOf.description: The last part of the match, shown in a warning colour.

TopicItem.description: `{"kind": "match", "data": {...}}`: the data sits in its own field so its fields can never clash with the tag.
